bib.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning

question: Can reflective natural-language prompt evolution adapt LLM systems to new tasks with far fewer rollouts than weight-space RL such as GRPO?
hypothesis: Language is a richer learning medium than sparse scalar rewards, so reflecting on trajectories in natural language yields larger gains per rollout than policy gradients.
contributions: GEPA, a reflective Pareto-based prompt optimizer for compound AI systems
Evaluation on six tasks with Qwen3 8B and GPT-4.1 Mini against GRPO, MIPROv2, TextGrad, Trace
Preliminary use as inference-time search for kernel code and for adversarial prompt search

method.summary: GEPA keeps a pool of prompt candidates for a multi-module LLM system. Each iteration it picks a candidate by sampling from the per-instance Pareto frontier, runs it on a minibatch of 3, has a reflection LM read traces plus textual feedback and rewrite one module's prompt (round-robin), keeps the child if the minibatch score improves, then scores it on the Pareto validation set. Optional Merge combines modules from two lineages.
method.task: prompt optimisation for compound AI systems (multi-hop QA, instruction following, privacy delegation, math)

prompts.text:
I provided an assistant with the following instructions to perform a task for me:
```
<current instruction>
```
The following are examples of different task inputs provided to the assistant along with the assistant's response for each of them, and some feedback on how the assistant's response could be better:
```
<Inputs, Outputs and Feedback for minibatch of examples>
```
Your task is to write a new instruction for the assistant.
Read the inputs carefully and identify the input format and infer detailed task description about the task I wish to solve with the assistant.
Read all the assistant responses and the corresponding feedback. Identify all niche and domain specific factual information about the task and include it in the instruction, as a lot of it may not be available to the assistant in the future. The assistant may have utilized a generalizable strategy to solve the task, if so, include that in the instruction as well.
Provide the new instructions within ``` blocks.

results.claim: Reflective instruction optimisation shows a lower generalisation gap than the exemplar-based finding of Wan et al. (2024).
results.quote: our results suggest that instructions generated by reflective prompt evolution can achieve stronger generalization

limits: No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; single numbers per cell.
GRPO beats GEPA on AIME-2025 (38.00 vs 32.00) with Qwen3 8B.
GEPA+Merge hurts Qwen3 8B; authors say hyperparameters were fixed across models and merge timing needs study.
Most GEPA rollouts are spent on validation scoring; authors propose smaller or dynamic validation sets as future work.
GRPO hyperparameters were explored manually (LR, beta, clipping) and the GRPO budget is a fixed 24,000 rollouts with LoRA for the main results.
Inference-time search (NPUEval, KernelBench) and adversarial search are preliminary.
Reflection LM identity is not given in the sections read.
GEPA needs a feedback function with textual traces; gains rely on it.
